extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense contracting officers, defense contractors, contract auditors (DCAA), and procurement officials
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for warranty clauses, correction of deficiencies, Contractor's Weighted Average Share in Cost Risk (CWAS) procedures, reporting, verification, recordkeeping, and acquisition/lease review rules for Automatic Data Processing Equipment (ADPE) in DoD contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Deficiencies — Contractor actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When supplies or services are nonconforming the contracting officer may require the contractor to: (i) obtain detailed recommendations for corrective action/instructions; (ii) (A) correct the supplies or services, or (B) replace the supplies or services — and if the contractor fails to furnish timely disposition the Contracting Officer may dispose of nonconforming supplies for the Contractor’s account; and (iii) obtain applicable data and reports and charge to the Contractor the cost occasioned to the Government thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CO disposes of nonconforming supplies for contractor’s account, Government entitled to reimbursement from the contractor or from proceeds for reasonable expenses of care and disposition and for excess costs incurred or to be incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Deficient Replacements and Re-performances
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplies or parts corrected or furnished in replacement and any services reperformed pursuant to the correction clause shall also be subject to all the provisions of the clause to the same extent as supplies or services initially accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repaired/replaced work is treated identically to original work under the clause; remedies preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example warranty clause for fixed-price construction contracts — contractor remedy obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor shall remedy at his own expense any failure of the work (including equipment) to conform to contract specifications and any defect of material, workmanship, or design in the work (excluding defects of any design furnished by the Government), provided Government gives notice promptly after discovery but not later than one year after final acceptance (or one year from date Government takes possession of part accepted prior to final acceptance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor must also remedy damage to equipment, site, buildings or contents resulting from such failure/defect and restore any work damaged in fulfilling the clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government remedy when contractor fails to correct
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the Contractor fail to remedy any such failure or defect within a reasonable time after receipt of notice, the Government shall have the right to replace, repair, or otherwise remedy such failure or defect at the Contractor’s expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This warranty shall not delay final acceptance of or final payment for the contract work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontractors' warranties enforcement by contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: All subcontractors', manufacturers' and suppliers' warranties and guaranties, express or implied, respecting any part of the work and any materials used therein shall be deemed obtained — and shall be enforced — by the Contractor as the agent and for the benefit of the Government without the necessity of separate transfer or assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If directed by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall require such subcontractors, manufacturers and suppliers to execute such warranties and guaranties in writing to the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repaired or replaced work subject to clause provisions and cumulative remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Any work repaired or replaced pursuant to the warranty clause shall also be subject to the provisions of the clause to the same extent as work originally performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rights and remedies of the Government provided in this clause are in addition to and do not limit any rights afforded to the Government by any other clause of this contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: CWAS — Scope of subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart sets forth the concepts and objectives which govern the Contractor’s Weighted Average Share in Cost Risk (CWAS) technique and detailed procedures for determining the contractor’s weighted average share for a given fiscal year as a percentage of costs incurred by type of contract during the contractor’s fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CWAS is intended to permit relaxation of administrative controls for contractors meeting verifiable thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: CWAS — General concept
rubrics_metrics.description: CWAS is based on measuring the degree of cost risk a contractor has assumed as evidenced by the mix of contract types he performs; contractors accepting higher risk contracts are more motivated to exercise prudent cost management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where contractors attain a verifiable weighted average share meeting prescribed thresholds, administrative controls and reasonableness overhead audits may be eliminated where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of the CWAS program
rubrics_metrics.description: Program objectives include: (a) furnish a measure of an individual contractor's risk motivation by contract types; (b) offer inducement to accept higher risk contracts; (c) minimize Government controls and reduce costs; (d) provide a simple, uniform procedure for equitable CWAS determination; (e) direct audit and management efforts to areas of greater Government risk; (f) provide basis for treating indirect costs as reasonable when CWAS rating is above threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single threshold level will be utilized for as many applications as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — CWAS
rubrics_metrics.description: CWAS is a technique for determining and expressing numerically the degree of cost risk a contractor has assumed, based on analysis of the mix of types of contracts he has agreed to perform; recognizes varying financial risk between contract types (e.g., CPFF = minimal risk, firm fixed-price = high risk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CWAS can be stated as a percentage of total costs incurred by contract type during the fiscal year; alternatives include use of cost of sales or sales basis where authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Costs incurred
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred consist of the contractor’s total cost input for his previous fiscal year identified through his method of accounting and reporting, representing all costs (whether or not allowable), including direct labor, direct material, subcontracts, direct services and properly allocated overhead, except as provided elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs must be categorized commercial vs Government business by contract types; treatment of production-for-stock and raw materials is addressed case-by-case with emphasis on practicality over precision and safeguards to prevent duplicate inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Profit center
rubrics_metrics.description: A profit center is the smallest organizationally independent segment charged with profit and loss responsibilities whose operations must absorb its indirect costs (generally a plant or division, but may vary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CWAS data may be developed company-wide or by profit center as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Threshold is the percentage designation at which a control or reasonableness test is relaxed or relieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds are established in applicable parts of the chapter for applying CWAS to administrative controls, overhead costs, and audit procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Government contracts (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this subpart, 'government contracts' includes only contracts with the U.S. Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of CWAS — voluntary participation and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: CWAS technique is applicable to all DoD contractors on a voluntary basis; a contractor desiring to participate may determine his own CWAS rating per procedures and submit costs-incurred data through appropriate channels for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors without DoD prime contracts may submit data to regional DCASR for qualification and application to subcontract efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of CWAS — withdrawal for fraud, misrepresentation or abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of CWAS principles may be withdrawn pursuant to a finding by the Administrative Contracting Officer of fraud, misrepresentation, or other abuse, effective only after written determination by the Head of a Procuring Activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal may apply to a profit center or entire corporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of CWAS — reinstatement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinstatement of CWAS with a contractor may occur only after the contractor has satisfactorily corrected the condition leading to withdrawal, submitted a complete statement of corrective actions to the ACO, and reapplied for a CWAS rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACO transmits recommendation to Head of Procuring Activity for determination before reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of CWAS — Secretary may deny or revoke in exceptional cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary having contract management cognizance may deny or revoke CWAS application where, due to special nature of contractor’s work, competitive position, future contracts, known procedures or unusual circumstances, CWAS ratings do not comparably/consistently reflect cost risk or provide assurance audit/controls are not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of CWAS — 35 percent minimum applicability rule
rubrics_metrics.description: CWAS technique shall not apply to any profit center where total dollar costs incurred for commercial work and Government competitive firm fixed-price contracts are less than 35 percent of total dollar costs incurred for all business at such profit center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures — data development and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors must submit required costs-incurred data at close of fiscal year to establish initial CWAS and must submit similar data annually thereafter; if company has multiple profit centers desiring qualification, develop data company-wide and for each profit center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any change in an accepted basis for computing CWAS ratings must be based on demonstrable organizational change or acceptable accounting structure change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures — contract types considered for contract mix
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of contracts to be considered are those authorized in Subpart D; for other approved types not listed, use factor/procedure for the most similar type in §3.1005(e); commercial contracts are assumed competitive and treated like competitive firm fixed-price contracts; subcontracts other than competitive FFP subcontracts under Government contracts cannot be classed as commercial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation method for CWAS rating
rubrics_metrics.description: For the fiscal year just ended: (1) determine total dollar costs incurred for commercial work and Government contract types; (2) multiply those costs by the approved percentage factor for each contract type to obtain 'dollar cost risk'; (3) total the dollar cost risks and divide by total dollar costs incurred — resulting percentage is CWAS rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contractor uses standard cost system, may elect to substitute cost of sales in lieu of costs incurred; sales basis may be authorized by Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage factors by contract type (CWAS table and special rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage factors are assigned by contract type (examples: cost-plus-incentive-fee 15%; fixed-price incentive (successive targets) 55%; fixed-price incentive (firm target) see table; firm fixed-price competitive 100%; commercial 100%; fixed-price with escalation noncompetitive/competitive 80%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules include: (2) letter-contract costs prior to definitization assigned zero factor; (3) 55% used for FPI (successive targets) until firm target negotiated; (4) FPI contract factors determined from ceiling-as-%-of-target table with interpolation, add 1 point for each 5% of contractor share above target, max 100, min contractor’s share; (5) competitive FFP and commercial costs may be combined at contractor option; (6) noncompetitive FFP defined as FFP contract/subcontract in excess of $1M awarded on basis of certified cost or pricing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter contract treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: All costs incurred prior to definitization of a letter contract shall be assigned a zero factor; costs incurred after definitization assigned factor applicable to definitive contract type. Date of definitization may be considered end of the month immediately prior to the date of definitization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-price incentive (FPI) factor computation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute ceiling price as percentage of target cost and apply interim factor from specified table (e.g., 110%->75, 115%->65, 120%->55, 125%->40, 130%+->15), interpolate for intermediate ceilings, add 1 point for each 5% of contractor share above target, use weighted average for multiple share rates; max contract factor 100, minimum is contractor’s share; increase factor by 10 points where FPI was awarded as result of price competition unless Secretary determines otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting procedure — submission, copies, and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor seeking initial CWAS approval shall prepare report with detailed cost-incurred data and computed CWAS ratings; original and two copies submitted to cognizant ACO (or DCASR if no DoD prime), and a copy to DCAA; to maintain approval submit similar report annually as soon as final fiscal year results available and no later than 105 days after fiscal year close unless ACO grants extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales basis authorization and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractor desiring CWAS computed on sales basis must obtain written authorization from the ACO before submitting sales-based report; request must be supported by data/rationale demonstrating substantially same results would be achieved under costs-incurred or sales basis; ACO with DCAA advice will authorize or disapprove; authorization remains until circumstances change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sales-basis CWAS rating is 5+ points above threshold and inventories stable, ACO may presume cost-basis computation will not differ meaningfully and waive further data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination and verification — ACO/DCAA timelines and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: ACO responsible for agreeing with contractor on CWAS rating and approving ratings. Within 30 days after receipt of contractor's report, DCAA auditor shall report to the ACO on validity of data and computation techniques or advise reasons for delay. ACO will promptly validate or reach agreement on revised rating. If ACO has not advised contractor within 60 days of receipt, the proposed CWAS will be considered approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assuming timely submission, prior fiscal-year CWAS rating will be applied to current year's operations pending ACO determination (subject to other rules on overhead reasonableness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative validation by independent public accountant
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of validation by DCAA, data related to commercial work and Government FFP contracts (or total CWAS proposal as agreed with ACO) will be accepted on basis of a report by an independent public accountant that the data is stated in accordance with the procedures and requirements set forth in this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of CWAS records and master register
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Defense Contract Administration Services Region shall maintain a current central register of CWAS ratings for contractors subject to ACO cognizance; copies of all CWAS ratings approved, withdrawn, or reinstated by regional ACOs forwarded to Headquarters, Defense Supply Agency (DSAH-F) where a master register is maintained and made available to contracting officers, auditors, and DoD personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADPE acquisition applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to all ADPE as defined in §1.201-29, except as components of end items to be delivered to the Government. If ADPE is purchased for the account of the Government or title will pass to the Government, acquisition must be approved as required by Part 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of decision to lease ADPE — required pre-approval actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If total cost of leasing ADPE is to be reimbursed under cost reimbursement contracts, contracting officer shall, prior to approval: (1) survey Defense Supply Agency for available excess ADPE (GFP) that could meet requirements; (2) determine whether leasing is appropriate under §15.205-48; (3) consider whether ADPE should be leased under a Federal Supply Schedule Contract; (4) require contractor to include a provision giving Government initial option to utilize any purchase or other benefits earned through rental payments (if rental authorized); (5) obtain approval of leasing arrangement from Senior ADPE policy official of Department/Agency which generated the requirement (noncompetitive leases forwarded to Assistant Secretary through Senior ADPE official).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADPE lease review thresholds and required actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If total cost of leasing ADPE in a single plant/division/cost center exceeds $500,000 per year and 50% or more of total cost is to be allocated to cost reimbursement contracts, the ACO should arrange for an initial review and an annual review of the contractor’s ADPE system to evaluate capability and need to continue leasing, and require contractor submission of proposed leases of new systems or major changes for advance determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major change is any addition or substitution of ADPE with annual cost in excess of $25,000. After reviews or proposed-lease review, ACO should enter an advance understanding per §15.107 or notify contractor of nonconcurrence and contemplated cost disallowance under §15.205-48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical ADP assistance to contracting officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical ADP assistance will be provided as necessary to the contracting officer by the Department having the preponderance of interest with the contractor.
